soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2 — certified computation
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem uses undeclared ε_tol rather than tol, and “level M” never fixes a tail radius, mesh/refinement schedule, quadrature precision, or validation predicate, so L_M and U_M are not yet determinate numerical functionals.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 2 — Zhou agreement frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: Its asserted iff makes agreement require divergence of artificial compactness slacks such as σ_j−σ_min and σ_max−σ_j, although a known positive scale on either calibration boundary is not an identification failure in Zhou et al.’s Theorem 7 or in the stated Gaussian experiment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Gaussian saddle and certified frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The result is conditional on the abstract known root-n radius, externally calibrated common cell scales, and maintained mechanism margins; it is not yet a sampled-data causal interval.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact honest connected-interval frontier conditional on each legal abstract Gaussian index ξ_G; the sampled-data lift remains a separate open construction.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 7 assumes P-Donsker evaluated influence functions, Assumptions 2–5, bounded Y, and nuisance-rate conditions, and concludes a centered root-n normal limit; §S17 proves it.
Theorem 5.4 describes smooth fibers as finite or as disjoint unions of polyhedra/manifolds with corners, while Theorem 5.8 describes singular fibers as unions of intersecting smooth manifolds.

The paper presents a Monte Carlo approximation to minimax expected-size confidence procedures via a finite supported convex class of priors and proves convergence to the corresponding Γ-minimax procedure.
The article establishes estimator distributions and uniform sizes of tests/confidence sets over drifting weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences for extremum-estimation settings.
The paper combines weak-identification limit theory with nondifferentiable parameter-boundary theory in minimum-distance models and proposes robust inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: Technical Report 617, revised May 2003; corroborative prepublication version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The checked version proves Bayes–minimax duality for weak-star compact confidence-procedure classes and gives the truncated-Pratt minimax solution for a bounded normal mean when τ≤2z_{1−α}.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the certified-scheme prose with a fully specified computable hierarchy indexed by M: rational tail bounds, mesh sizes, quadrature error budgets, exact validation inequalities, and identify ε_tol with tol.

Revise the Zhou-agreement OEQ so its frontier contains only identification-relevant inverse/label-separation coordinates; either prove a distinct boundary effect for the compactness slacks or remove them from the necessary condition.

Promote the saddle from an abstract benchmark to a stronger field contribution by adding a theorem that compares it with at least two named weak-identification interval constructions on an explicit shared submodel.

recommended_next_step: Revise the determinate certificate construction and the overbroad agreement-frontier iff, then retain the conditional Gaussian-saddle kernel for Stage 0.
